" Beaches are dynamic , and need to be monitored and -- if necessary -- refurbished . <p> " But we 're all fairly sure that without the gas terminal being where it is , we 'd be in the same situation as many of our neighbours along the coast . " <p> " Local governments are struggling and overspent with their budgets , but if we ca n't save the coastline we should at least compensate people properly for the home that they 've lost . <p> " But compensating somebody at the price their house is worth when it 's teetering on the brink of collapse is not sufficient for them to be able to relocate somewhere else . I think the Government needs to step up . " <p> Frenchie adds : " I think it 's very difficult for people to accept the economics when it 's their homes , their livelihoods and their futures . <p> " To be told ' you 're not worth that ' ... the sea will do what it will do at the end of the day , but that 's a bitter pill to swallow . " <p> Outside the Kingfisher , Harry Blathwayt , a district councillor in charge of all things coastal , explained the economics behind the current Government policy . <p> " An economist basically looks at this and says , for example , that the Mundesley and Cromer scheme -- where ? 25m has been spent this year delivering rock armour to protect the two towns ' coasts -- is spread across a larger expanse of homes and businesses and that 's why it is receiving defences . <p> " We 've got to look at the value of strategic land , heritage assets , everything else as well as houses . <p> " But obviously you still get a bigger bang for your buck if you protect places where there 're more homes as opposed to smaller villages like Happisburgh . " <p> The fact there is no compensatory or insurance schemes for coastal erosion has " got to change , " he said , adding : " I 'm not happy ; the current policy is not something I like , but it 's not a local government policy -- it is the national government . " <p> Happisburgh Lighthouse seen through the rooftops on Beach Road ( Photo : Max Tobin ) <h> A centuries-old problem , rapidly worsening <p> Eroding coasts are nothing new and to some degree are necessary to replenish beaches elsewhere along a coastline . <p> But Dr Garcia warns that due to human interventions -- or a lack thereof -- and sea level rises caused by global warming , the scale of the issue will escalate rapidly . <h> Read Next <p> " We know that what we 're seeing today is certainly something we will see more often in the future , " he said . <p> Meanwhile , a recent report by the Environment Agency found that over six million properties in England are currently at risk of flooding , with this number expected to increase to eight million -- or one in four properties -- by 2050 . <p> Without sufficient investment , the report found that current coastal erosion risks are also likely to increase " significantly " over the coming century . <p> A new National Coastal Erosion Risk Map ( NCERM ) , updated for the first time since 2017 , is set to be released by the EA early next year , allowing both property owners and decision makers to view the projected implications of climate change on erosion risk for the first time . <p> Campaigners like One Home founder Angela Terry told The i Paper the " shocking " new data from the NCERM publication -- which has been pushed back several times despite it being crucial to informing both current and prospective coastal dwellers of the future risks they face -- would be a " huge story " . <p> A Defra spokesperson said the Government is " committed to supporting coastal communities and making sure flood risk management is fit for the challenges we face now and in the future . " <p> They added : " That is why this Government will invest ? 2.4bn over the next two years to better protect communities from flooding and coastal erosion . <p> " Our newly established Flood Resilience Taskforce will also improve resilience and preparation across central government and local authorities to protect communities across the UK . " <p> Further decisions on funding for coastal erosion beyond 2026/27 are expected to be made during the Spending Review , which concludes next June -- but Chancellor Rachel Reeves has asked all government departments to identify 5 per cent " efficiency savings " as part of a review to set their budgets for the coming years . <h> Possible solutions : what can be done ? <p> There 's a risk that hard defences such as sea walls may end up hampering natural beach and cliff re-shaping processes that could even help limit cliff erosion in the long run , Dr Garcia explains . <p> " If you completely stop the cliff from eroding , you kind of starve the coast of sediment and then there 's no other sources of sediment to keep putting up lines of defence , " he added . <p> Proposing another possible solution , he continued : " There is a willingness to use solutions like artificial nourishment to protect our coasts , but sediment is not an infinite resource . <p> But what if there were to be a sort of ' circular economy ' , he asks . <p> " If you lose your land from the cliff eroding , but that same sand will widen the beach somewhere else , what is the value to those benefitting ? If you have to pay for that , how much it would cost ? Can you make a budget , so the people who are benefiting from that wider beach can contribute to a pot of money and the people who are losing their land can then use that money to relocate somewhere else ? <p> " That 's an innovative idea that I 've never seen anywhere else before . @@119482964 <p> Jimmy Carter had a firm handshake and eyes that sparkled with just a hint of mischief . <p> It was March 2004 and America'a 39th president had just published one of the several dozen books he authored over the course of his lifetime , this one entitled The Hornet 's Nest : A Novel of the Revolutionary War . <p> The invitation to talk with him at the Carter Centre in Atlanta , Georgia , was to publicise the book , and we were told that was the only subject he wished to discuss . <p> We were hoping he might be persuaded to talk about other topics , in particular the invasion of Iraq , which had been launched a year earlier by George W Bush and Tony Blair , but had already revealed it was not going to be the quick , clean , conquest the two leaders believed it would be . <p> It had also become clear Saddam Hussein had not possessed weapons of mass destruction , as the two Western leaders had claimed as their main justification for an invasion many believed illegal . <p> Truth be told , I was rather intimidated and utterly nervous , while trying and failing to disguise it . No matter one 's personal views of his time in office , here sitting opposite me was a former president of the United States . <p> And so I tried to play it cool , while Carter just emitted warmth . He must have been questioned by thousands of reporters . For me , he is the only leader of such stature I 've interviewed during my career . <p> Carter addresses the audience after being awarded the Order of Manuel Amador Guerrero by Panama 's president in 2016 ( Photo : John Bazemore/AP ) <p> I 'd gone equipped with a newly purchased digital recorder , but did not trust it . So , as I do today , I made copious shorthand notes as we spoke over the course of half an hour . <p> I realised I could not raise the issue of Iraq immediately . Even though Carter had left the White House more than two decades earlier -- beaten in a landslide by Republican Ronald Reagan in 1980 -- it was not common or customary for ex-presidents to criticise the actions of their predecessors . <p> So I started by asking about the War of Independence . Were there any lessons that could be drawn from the conflict by which America secured its independence from Britain to the events of the present day , I asked ? <h> Read Next <p> And what about the present day ? " Most wars , certainly not all , could have been avoided , " he said . " There was no reason for us to become involved in Iraq last year . That was a war based on lies and misinterpretations from London and Washington , claiming falsely that Saddam Hussein was responsible for 9/11 , claiming falsely that Iraq had weapons of mass destruction . " <p> He said Bush " was inclined to finish a war that his father had precipitated against Iraq " . <p> At that moment , I realised I had my scoop . I hoped Carter had not sensed my beaming smile , though of course he was fully aware of the significance of what he was saying to a reporter and what any journalist would do with his comments . <p> Sun flooded through the windows . In the entrance were leaflets that outlined the centre 's work to tackle river blindness in Guatemala , and against guinea worm disease in more than 20 African and Asian nations . <p> The Carter Centre has over the years sent observers to more than 100 elections around the world , and more recently worked to support elections in the US . <p> These days it has become commonplace for politicians to talk of their opponents and rivals in terms utterly without precedent . No one is more guilty of this than Donald Trump , whose insults and attacks are so frequently and unnecessarily levelled , people become all but numb to them , and his way of operating almost normalised . <p> Because what Carter was doing 20 years ago was so uncommon , his words had all the more power . <p> He was often the target for Trump 's attacks , insulting him as a means of attacking Joe Biden , and claiming the man who grew up dirt poor in Plains , Georgia , would be happy as Americans were no longer ranking him as the worst of their chief executives . <p> In truth , Carter 's reputation has long been on the mend , in part because in many of the topics he devoted effort to -- tackling climate change , getting more women judges on the bench , addressing social inequality -- he has been shown to have been ahead of his time . <p> When , in 2023 , pollster Gallup asked Americans to retrospectively evaluate Carter 's presidency , 57 per cent said they approved of the job he did , and 36 per cent disapproved . That would place him in lower half of presidents , better than Richard Nixon and Trump , and similar to George W Bush and Bill Clinton . <p> Ironically , one of the things Carter viewed as a lasting achievement were the Torrijos-Carter Treaties , which gave Panama control of the Panama Canal . <p> In recent days , president-elect Trump has been vowing to tear up the documents and demand the canal 's return . " We 're being ripped off at the Panama Canal like we 're being ripped off everywhere else , " Trump claimed at an Arizona rally last week . <p> In our conversation , there was no reason for the subject of Trump to come up . It feels fair to say , based on what Carter has said publicly about him , he did not think very warmly of the New Yorker . <p> In 2019 , Carter said he did not believe Trump would have won the 2016 election without Russian " interference " . Speaking ahead of the 2020 election he said : " I think it will be a disaster to have four more years of Trump . " <p> " The challenges Jimmy faced as President came at a pivotal time for our country and he did everything in his power to improve the lives of all Americans , " said the incoming president . " For that , we all owe him a debt of gratitude. "
